- Validate input: ensure xs has even length, highest-degree coefficient nonzero; handle trivial constant/linear cases directly (return -xs[0]/xs[1] for length 2).
- Use a robust root-finding method for real root: bracket a sign change by scanning over an expanding range (e.g., powers of two) evaluating poly; once a bracket [a,b] with f(a)*f(b) ≤ 0 is found, apply bisection (or secant) until tolerance, returning the root.
- Leverage poly(xs, x) for evaluation; set max iterations and tolerance; if no bracket found within limits, raise an error, but given constraints expect at least one real root so expand range sufficiently (e.g., up to large bound).
